name: ACP-105

angle.text: ACP-105 is a partial-agonist SARM that users take hoping for lean mass gain with milder androgenic effects. It improved anabolic markers in castrated rats and mice; there are no human trials, and it is sold online as a research chemical.

summary: A discontinued experimental SARM tested in rats and mice; no human trials, sold online as a research chemical.
note: Preclinical only; banned in sport; no human safety data.
currentQuick:
ACP-105 is an experimental SARM from the late 2000s. Rodent studies showed muscle-related effects and some cognitive findings.
No human trials were found; it is unapproved.
How it works: It acts as a partial agonist at the androgen receptor, producing smaller effects than testosterone in tissues tested in rats.
Risks and caveats: Human safety is unknown. SARMs as a class are banned in sport and have been linked in reports to liver injury and hormone suppression.
deepLead:
ACP-105 is an investigational nonsteroidal selective androgen receptor modulator (SARM) with partial agonist activity relative to testosterone, described in a 2009 Journal of Medicinal Chemistry paper . It was discovered through a high-throughput screen using receptor selection and amplification technology, and improved anabolic parameters in castrated male rats .
Later animal work examined it in models of cognitive decline and radiation-related deficits . It is not approved; SARMs are banned in sport, and metabolism studies in humans-targeted and equine doping control have been published .

name: AC-262536

angle.text: AC-262,536 is a SARM that users take in pursuit of lean muscle gain. It improved anabolic parameters in castrated rats in a two-week study; human muscle effects are untested, and it is sold as a research chemical.

summary: An Acadia-developed experimental SARM with rat data and no human trials, sold online as a research chemical.
note: Preclinical only; unapproved; banned in sport.
currentQuick:
AC-262536 is an experimental SARM from Acadia Pharmaceuticals. Rat studies showed muscle-building effects with smaller prostate effects than testosterone.
It has never been tested in a published human trial.
How it works: It is a partial agonist of the androgen receptor with reported tissue selectivity in rats.
Risks and caveats: Human safety is unknown. As an unapproved SARM it is banned in sport, and the class is linked in reports to liver injury and hormone suppression.
deepLead:
AC-262,536 (also called Accadrine) is an investigational nonsteroidal selective androgen receptor modulator developed by Acadia Pharmaceuticals, described in a 2008 pharmacological characterisation as a potent, selective androgen receptor ligand with partial agonist activity . In a 2-week study in castrated male rats it improved anabolic parameters .
Wikipedia reports that its maximal effect on levator ani muscle weight was about 66% of testosterone's versus about 27% for prostate weight . It has not been approved and no human trial was identified; it appeared as a designer drug sold online by at least 2020 .

name: BMS-564929

angle.text: BMS-564929 is a highly potent SARM mentioned by muscle-building users for its strong muscle effect with little prostate stimulation in rats. It was developed for age-related decline and stalled in early trials, so its use for physique rests on rat data.

summary: A very potent Bristol-Myers Squibb SARM that stalled in early trials; rat data only.
note: Trial discontinued; strong LH suppression reported; banned in sport.
currentQuick:
BMS-564929 is a highly potent experimental SARM built by Bristol-Myers Squibb for age-related muscle and hormone decline.
Rat results were striking, but the early human trial was discontinued and no results are public.
How it works: It binds the androgen receptor very tightly, driving muscle growth in rats while stimulating the prostate less.
Risks and caveats: Human safety is unpublished. It suppresses luteinizing hormone strongly, is unapproved and is banned in sport.
deepLead:
BMS-564929 (also PS-178990) is a potent, orally active, nonsteroidal selective androgen receptor modulator developed by Bristol-Myers Squibb for age-related functional decline in men . A 2007 Endocrinology study reported a subnanomolar androgen receptor affinity, selectivity over other steroid receptors, and strong stimulation of skeletal muscle with comparatively little prostate stimulation in castrated rats .
It advanced to early clinical trials, but Wikipedia reports that the Phase I trial was discontinued, and no results were identified . It is unapproved and SARMs are prohibited in sport .

name: GLPG0492

angle.text: GLPG0492 is a non-steroidal SARM that users take hoping to build muscle with weaker effects on the prostate. It was tested in mouse muscle-wasting models and phase 1 volunteer trials; efficacy in people is not shown.

summary: Experimental non-steroidal SARM tested in mouse muscle-wasting models and phase 1 volunteer trials; no efficacy data in people.
note: Not an approved drug; no published human efficacy data.
currentQuick:
GLPG0492 is an experimental selective androgen receptor modulator (SARM) that was developed to build muscle with less effect on the prostate and other reproductive tissue than testosterone. It has been studied for muscle-wasting conditions such as sarcopenia, cachexia and muscular dystrophy.
Research so far consists of rodent studies and three phase 1 trials in healthy volunteers. No published trial has measured whether it changes muscle or appearance in people.
How it works: It binds the androgen receptor as a partial agonist. In rodents it increased muscle-related measures and strength with reduced effects on reproductive organs compared with testosterone-type comparators.
Risks and caveats: Human safety data are not summarized in published sources reviewed. It is not approved for any use, and SARMs as a class are subject to anti-doping testing.
deepLead:
GLPG0492, also known as DT-200, is an experimental non-steroidal selective androgen receptor modulator (SARM) of the diarylhydantoin chemical class. It was designed to promote muscle growth through the androgen receptor while having weaker effects on reproductive tissues such as the prostate, and it has been investigated for muscle-wasting conditions including sarcopenia, cachexia and muscular dystrophy.
The compound was identified through medicinal chemistry work on hydantoin-based androgen receptor ligands and was reported in a rat model to have anabolic activity on muscle that was dissociated from androgenic activity on the prostate. Later studies in mice examined its effects in a muscular dystrophy model and in hindlimb immobilization.
Published human efficacy data are not available: registered phase 1 studies in healthy volunteers have been completed, but no clinical trial in a muscle-wasting condition is listed among the sources reviewed. The compound is not approved for any use. It is also one of several SARMs for which laboratory detection methods have been developed for doping control.

name: TFM-4AS-1

chain: Favors muscle and bone in rats
angle.text: TFM-4AS-1 is a steroidal SARM that muscle-building readers cite for favoring muscle and bone over reproductive tissue in rats. It has never been tested in people, so its physique use rests on laboratory work.

summary: Laboratory steroidal SARM shown in rats to favor muscle and bone over reproductive tissue; never tested in people.
note: Preclinical only; no human data.
currentQuick:
TFM-4AS-1 is a lab-stage steroidal SARM first described in 2009. In rats it increased muscle and bone while having smaller effects on reproductive organs and oil-producing skin glands than a related full agonist.
No human study of it was found.
How it works: It partially activates the androgen receptor and blocks the receptor's internal N/C-terminal interaction, so it switches on only some androgen-responsive genes.
Risks and caveats: Human safety is unknown. It is not approved for any use.
deepLead:
TFM-4AS-1 is an experimental steroidal selective androgen receptor modulator (SARM) described in a 2009 paper in the Journal of Biological Chemistry. It belongs to the 4-aza-steroid class and was characterized as a potent androgen receptor ligand that only partially activates the receptor.
In that study, ovariectomized rats given TFM-4AS-1 gained bone and muscle mass while showing reduced effects on reproductive organs and sebaceous glands, and the compound did not promote prostate growth. The sources reviewed contain no human studies of TFM-4AS-1, and it has no approved use.

name: MK-0773

angle.text: MK-0773 is a steroidal SARM tested for sarcopenia, where it added lean mass in frail older women. It did not improve strength or function in that phase 2 trial, and users interested in physique follow it as a human-data example.

summary: Steroidal SARM that added lean mass in frail older women but did not improve strength or function in a phase 2 trial.
note: Investigational only; lean mass gain did not translate to function in the one efficacy trial.
currentQuick:
MK-0773 is an investigational SARM that was tested for sarcopenia, the loss of muscle with age. It was designed to act on muscle with less effect on other tissues.
In the one published efficacy trial, 170 older women gained lean mass compared with placebo, but strength and physical function did not improve beyond placebo.
How it works: It is a steroidal androgen receptor ligand picked from a large screen of compounds for partial, tissue-selective activity.
Risks and caveats: Safety data from the efficacy trial are not detailed in the sources reviewed. It is not approved for any use and is covered by anti-doping testing.
deepLead:
MK-0773, also known as PF-05314882, is an experimental steroidal selective androgen receptor modulator (SARM) that was developed to increase muscle mass and strength while minimizing effects on other tissues. It was tested in clinical trials for sarcopenia, the age-related loss of muscle mass and function.
Its discovery was reported in 2010 as the product of a screening strategy using more than 1,000 synthetic androgen receptor ligands to look for compounds whose anabolic and reproductive-tissue effects were separable. In a phase 2A trial in 170 frail older women with sarcopenia, it increased lean body mass compared with placebo, but this did not translate into improved strength or physical function. The compound is not approved for any use.

name: GSK2881078

chain: Gain in lean mass and leg strength
angle.text: GSK2881078 is a SARM that raised lean mass in older adults and leg strength in men with COPD, so muscle-focused readers cite it as one of the better human data sets. Trials were in ill or older people, not people seeking a cosmetic physique.

summary: Pharma-developed SARM that raised lean mass in older adults and leg strength in men with COPD, at the cost of lower HDL and transient liver-enzyme rises.
note: Investigational; HDL lowering and ALT elevations reported in trials.
currentQuick:
GSK2881078 is a non-steroidal SARM that GlaxoSmithKline tested for muscle weakness in chronic illness. In healthy older men and women it produced dose-dependent gains in lean mass over placebo.
In a 13-week trial in people with COPD it increased leg strength in men beyond exercise alone, though patient-reported outcomes did not change.
How it works: It acts on the androgen receptor to promote muscle growth and has a very long half-life, reported at over 100 hours.
Risks and caveats: Trials reported lowered HDL cholesterol and sex hormone-binding globulin, transient ALT elevations and, in one case, a drug rash. It is not approved, and SARM safety reviews cite liver injury and tendon rupture cases with recreational SARM use generally.
deepLead:
GSK2881078 is an investigational non-steroidal selective androgen receptor modulator (SARM) developed by GlaxoSmithKline for muscle weakness associated with chronic and acute illness. It has been tested in phase 1 and phase 2 trials, including studies in healthy older adults and in people with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD).
Trials found dose-dependent increases in lean mass, and in men with COPD a gain in leg strength beyond exercise alone. Reported safety findings included reductions in HDL cholesterol and sex hormone-binding globulin, and transient rises in liver enzyme (ALT) levels. It is not approved for any use.

name: OPK-88004

angle.text: OPK-88004 is a SARM that raised lean mass and reduced fat in prostate cancer survivors, which is the body-composition change followers of SARMs look for. Symptoms and performance did not improve in that trial, and it has not been studied for appearance.

summary: Investigational SARM that raised lean mass and cut fat in prostate cancer survivors without improving symptoms or performance.
note: Investigational only; oral SARMs suppress HDL cholesterol.
currentQuick:
OPK-88004 is an experimental SARM tested in testosterone-deficient prostate cancer survivors and in men with BPH. In the survivor trial it increased lean mass and lowered fat mass.
It did not improve sexual symptoms or physical performance, and the BPH trial was terminated.
How it works: It is an oral non-steroidal androgen receptor modulator intended to act on muscle with less effect on the prostate.
Risks and caveats: The survivor trial reported no PSA recurrence or erythrocytosis. Oral SARMs have been reported to suppress HDL cholesterol. It is not approved for any use.
deepLead:
OPK-88004, also known as LY-2452473, is an investigational non-steroidal selective androgen receptor modulator (SARM). It has been studied for androgen deficiency symptoms in prostate cancer survivors and for benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH).
In a randomized trial of 114 testosterone-deficient men who had undergone prostatectomy for low-grade prostate cancer, it increased lean body mass and reduced fat mass, but did not improve sexual symptoms or physical performance, and no PSA recurrence was seen. A phase 2 BPH trial was terminated. It is not approved for any use.

name: MK-3984

angle.text: MK-3984 is an obscure SARM that muscle-building communities occasionally list as a lean-mass candidate. Little is published beyond a doping-control metabolite study in zebrafish, and there are no human data.

summary: Obscure SARM candidate with no human data; known mainly from a doping-control metabolite study.
note: No clinical data found.
currentQuick:
MK-3984 is a little-documented SARM candidate aimed at muscle and bone. The only dedicated study found maps its metabolism in zebrafish for doping control.
No human trials were found.
How it works: As a SARM it is designed to act on androgen receptors in muscle and bone, though no mechanism data specific to it were found.
Risks and caveats: Human safety is unknown, and it is not approved for any use.
deepLead:
MK-3984 is an experimental selective androgen receptor modulator (SARM) targeting muscle and bone tissue. Very little published information exists: it is mentioned in the SARM literature  and has been the subject of a 2026 doping-control study of its metabolism in zebrafish.
No clinical trials or human data were found, and it is not approved for any use.

name: Arcarine

angle.text: Arcarine (ORM-11984) is a SARM from Orion that muscle-building readers know as a discontinued candidate for selective muscle activation. It reached Phase I and left almost no public data on muscle or appearance.

summary: Orion's discontinued SARM candidate; reached Phase I and left almost no public data on muscle or looks.
note: Investigational only; never approved, with no published human efficacy data.
currentQuick:
Arcarine (ORM-11984) is a selective androgen receptor modulator that Orion Corporation developed for conditions such as benign prostatic hyperplasia, hypogonadism and osteoporosis.
It reached Phase I trials before development was discontinued. It is not a marketed product, and no human data on muscle or appearance outcomes have been published.
How it works: As a SARM, it was designed to activate androgen receptors in tissues like muscle and bone while having weaker effects on the prostate. Its structure was never disclosed, and a rat study of local delivery reported it did not act as an anabolic agent in that model.
Risks and caveats: No safety data are published. SARMs as a class are unapproved, banned by WADA, and have been linked in case reports to liver injury with recreational use.
deepLead:
Arcarine (development code ORM-11984) is an investigational selective androgen receptor modulator (SARM) developed by the Finnish company Orion Corporation. SARMs are drugs designed to activate the androgen receptor in some tissues, such as muscle and bone, more than in others, such as the prostate .
Arcarine was studied for benign prostatic hyperplasia, hypogonadism and osteoporosis. It reached Phase I clinical trials, after which development was discontinued, and its chemical structure has not been disclosed . Published information is sparse, and no trial results for appearance or muscle-building use are available.

name: GSK-971086

angle.text: GSK-971086 is an indole-class SARM that was investigated for sarcopenia and androgen deficiency, and is followed by muscle-building readers as a lean-mass candidate. It never got past Phase I, and no efficacy data exist.

summary: A discontinued GSK indole-class SARM that never got past Phase I; no efficacy data exist.
note: Investigational only; not approved and no published efficacy results.
currentQuick:
GSK-971086 is an experimental SARM from GlaxoSmithKline that was studied for sarcopenia and androgen deficiency.
It was tested in a single Phase I safety trial in healthy men and then discontinued. It is not a marketed drug.
How it works: SARMs aim to switch on androgen receptors selectively, favoring muscle and bone over reproductive tissues. This compound belongs to the indole chemical class.
Risks and caveats: No results from its Phase I trial are public in the sources reviewed. The SARM class is unapproved, banned in sport by WADA, and linked in case reports to liver injury with recreational use.
deepLead:
GSK-971086 (also written GSK971086) is an investigational non-steroidal selective androgen receptor modulator (SARM) from the indole chemical class, developed by GlaxoSmithKline and investigated for sarcopenia (age-related muscle loss) and androgen deficiency .
A Phase I trial registered in 2007 tested safety, tolerability and blood levels in healthy adult males after a single dose and after seven days of dosing . Development was discontinued after Phase I . No results for appearance or muscle-building have been published in the sources reviewed.

name: GSK-2849466

angle.text: GSK-2849466 is a SARM that was investigated for cachexia and heart failure, and muscle-focused readers note it as a lean-mass candidate. Development stopped after one small Phase I trial, so appearance effects are untested.

summary: A GSK SARM candidate for cachexia that stopped after one small Phase I trial.
note: Investigational only; no published efficacy results.
currentQuick:
GSK-2849466 is an experimental SARM from GlaxoSmithKline, studied for cachexia and heart failure.
It was tested in one small Phase I trial of 17 healthy men and then discontinued.
How it works: It is meant to activate androgen receptors preferentially in muscle and bone rather than reproductive tissue, and belongs to the N-arylhydroxyalkyl class.
Risks and caveats: No trial results are published in the sources reviewed. The SARM class is unapproved, banned by WADA, and associated in case reports with liver injury from recreational use.
deepLead:
GSK-2849466 (GSK2849466) is an investigational non-steroidal selective androgen receptor modulator (SARM) of the N-arylhydroxyalkyl class, developed by GlaxoSmithKline and investigated for cachexia and heart failure .
A Phase I trial begun in 2012 evaluated its safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics in 17 healthy male subjects . Development was discontinued after Phase I . No appearance-related data are available.

name: GTx-027

angle.text: GTx-027 is a SARM explored for breast cancer and stress urinary incontinence, and is occasionally listed by muscle-building readers among SARMs. It is essentially preclinical, with no data on muscle or appearance.

summary: A SARM candidate explored for breast cancer and incontinence; essentially preclinical, with nothing on looks.
note: Investigational only; no human efficacy data.
currentQuick:
GTx-027 is an experimental SARM of the arylpropionamide class, investigated for breast cancer and stress urinary incontinence.
It is described as discontinued or preclinical, and no human trial on muscle or appearance has been published.
How it works: SARMs are designed to activate androgen receptors selectively. Mouse research on SARMs reported increased pelvic floor muscle mass.
Risks and caveats: No human safety data are available in the sources reviewed. The SARM class is unapproved, banned by WADA, and linked in case reports to liver injury with recreational use.
deepLead:
GTx-027 is an investigational non-steroidal selective androgen receptor modulator (SARM) of the arylpropionamide class, associated with GTx, Inc. and investigated for breast cancer and stress urinary incontinence . Wikipedia lists its status as Phase I, discontinued, or preclinical .
Published research on the compound is limited. A 2017 mouse study examined whether tissue-selective SARMs increase pelvic floor muscle mass in ovariectomized mice, motivated by the lack of oral treatments for stress urinary incontinence . No appearance or physique trials exist.

name: LY305

angle.text: LY305 is a SARM built as a transdermal treatment for low testosterone, which makes it of interest to those seeking a muscle and hormone-related physique. It was also explored for muscle wasting; there are no appearance data.

summary: A skin-applied SARM built for low testosterone; interesting pharmacology, no appearance data.
note: Investigational only; not approved.
currentQuick:
LY305 is an experimental SARM designed to be applied through the skin for men with low testosterone, and explored for muscle wasting and osteoporosis.
It is not an approved product, and no study has tested it for appearance outcomes.
How it works: It activates the androgen receptor and was engineered for skin absorption and strong liver clearance, to limit liver exposure to the parent compound.
Risks and caveats: Little human safety data is public. SARMs are unapproved and banned by WADA, and a 2025 study characterized its metabolism to help doping control.
deepLead:
LY305 is an investigational non-steroidal selective androgen receptor modulator (SARM) of the N-arylhydroxyalkyl class, developed as a transdermal (through-the-skin) treatment for hypogonadism, and also explored for muscle wasting and osteoporosis .
A 2018 paper described it as bioavailable by the transdermal route while being cleared extensively by the liver, a design intended to limit liver exposure to the parent compound . Wikipedia reports promising results in a Phase I trial . No appearance-related trials have been published.

name: PF-06260414

angle.text: PF-06260414 is Pfizer's oral SARM, studied for cachexia and tested for safety in healthy men. It was shelved after Phase I, and muscle-building readers follow it only as a candidate without appearance data.

summary: Pfizer's oral SARM for cachexia; safety-tested in healthy men, then shelved.
note: Investigational only; no efficacy trials.
currentQuick:
PF-06260414 is an experimental oral SARM from Pfizer, studied for cachexia.
It completed a Phase I safety and pharmacokinetic study in healthy men, and development was then discontinued.
How it works: It is designed to activate androgen receptors preferentially in muscle and bone, and belongs to the isoquinoline class.
Risks and caveats: Only Phase I tolerability data exist, and efficacy was never tested in trials. The SARM class is unapproved and banned by WADA, with case reports of liver injury from recreational use.
deepLead:
PF-06260414 is an investigational non-steroidal selective androgen receptor modulator (SARM) of the isoquinoline class, developed by Pfizer and investigated for cachexia; development was discontinued after Phase I .
A 2016 paper reported tolerability, pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic results from single and multiple ascending oral doses in healthy subjects . It has not been tested for appearance or physique outcomes.

name: JNJ-26146900

angle.text: JNJ-26146900 is a SARM investigated for prostate cancer and noted by muscle-building readers for its androgen receptor selectivity. It was tested only in rats and never in humans, so its appearance use is untested.

summary: A Johnson & Johnson SARM tested only in rats for prostate cancer; never given to humans.
note: Preclinical only; no human data exist.
currentQuick:
JNJ-26146900 is an experimental SARM that Johnson & Johnson studied as a possible prostate cancer drug. It was never marketed.
In rats it shrank prostate tumors and limited castration-related bone loss. No human trials have been published, and nothing is known about any muscle or appearance effect in people.
How it works: It binds the androgen receptor and acts differently in different tissues: antagonist-like in the prostate, with anabolic effects reported in muscle and bone in animals.
Risks and caveats: Human safety has not been studied. It is not approved for any use.
deepLead:
JNJ-26146900 is an experimental nonsteroidal selective androgen receptor modulator (SARM) developed by Johnson & Johnson, investigated as a possible prostate cancer treatment. It has never been marketed and, according to Wikipedia, was never tested in humans.
In a 2007 rat study, the compound bound the androgen receptor with modest affinity and behaved as an antagonist in a cell-based assay, similar to bicalutamide, while showing tissue-selective effects in animals: it reduced prostate weight and prostate tumor size and prevented some of the bone loss that follows castration. Because it is a SARM-class research compound, it is occasionally mentioned in muscle-building discussions, but no human appearance or muscle data exist.

name: RU-59063

angle.text: RU-59063 is a 1990s research androgen-receptor ligand, sometimes classed as a SARM, and became a template for later antiandrogens. It has no human use, and its appearance link in muscle circles is theoretical.

summary: A 1990s research androgen-receptor ligand that became a template for later antiandrogens; no human use.
note: Laboratory compound only; no human data.
currentQuick:
RU-59063 is an early nonsteroidal compound that binds the androgen receptor very tightly. It was studied in laboratories and never marketed.
Its main significance is as a chemical template for later prostate cancer drugs and imaging agents. No studies of muscle or appearance effects in people exist.
How it works: It occupies the androgen receptor with higher affinity than testosterone, acting with mixed antagonist and weak agonist behaviour.
Risks and caveats: Human safety is unstudied and it has no approved use.
deepLead:
RU-59063 is an experimental nonsteroidal androgen, sometimes classed as a SARM, first described in 1994. It was never marketed and has no clinical use.
It was derived from the antiandrogen nilutamide and bound the rat androgen receptor with very high affinity, reported as up to about three times that of testosterone, with little binding to other steroid receptors. Later work showed dose-dependent androgenic activity. It served mainly as a starting point for later antiandrogens such as enzalutamide and apalutamide, and for radioligand research.

name: Bolandiol

angle.text: Bolandiol is a nandrolone-related steroid with mixed androgen, estrogen and progestin activity, discussed by physique-focused readers as an anabolic. It was studied in rats and never marketed as a base; human appearance data are lacking.

summary: A nandrolone-related steroid with mixed androgen, estrogen and progestin activity; studied in rats, never marketed as a base.
note: WADA-prohibited; reported to show no strength or body-composition effect in clinical studies per Wikipedia.
currentQuick:
Bolandiol is a nandrolone-like anabolic steroid. Its dipropionate ester has been marketed in the past, but the base compound never was.
In castrated rats it raised lean mass and bone density. Wikipedia reports clinical studies found no change in strength, body composition or performance.
How it works: It binds the androgen receptor weakly but also has estrogenic and progestational activity, and it suppresses gonadotropins and endogenous testosterone.
Risks and caveats: It suppresses natural testosterone production in animals. It is on the WADA prohibited list.
deepLead:
Bolandiol (19-nor-4-androstenediol, estr-4-ene-3beta,17beta-diol) is a synthetic anabolic-androgenic steroid related to nandrolone. The base compound was never marketed, though its dipropionate ester (anabiol) has been sold. The World Anti-Doping Agency lists it as prohibited.
Animal research describes it as unusual among anabolic steroids because it has androgenic, estrogenic and progestational activity. In castrated adult male rats it increased lean mass and bone mineral density without strongly stimulating sex accessory glands. Wikipedia states that several clinical studies concluded it did not change strength, body composition or exercise performance, although the source studies are not in the cited literature reviewed here.

name: Dienolone

angle.text: Dienolone is a nandrolone-like steroid that physique readers mention for its anabolic class. It was developed as RU-3118 and never marketed, and is mainly of interest as a chemical intermediate; human muscle effects are untested.

summary: A never-marketed nandrolone-like steroid, mainly of interest as a chemical intermediate.
note: No human studies; sources are thin.
currentQuick:
Dienolone is a 19-nortestosterone steroid developed under the code RU-3118 and never sold as a drug.
Sources describe its receptor affinities in animal tissue and its role as a synthesis intermediate; no human data exist.
How it works: It binds androgen and progesterone receptors slightly less strongly than nandrolone in animal tissue assays.
Risks and caveats: Human safety is unstudied.
deepLead:
Dienolone (also nordienolone, RU-3118, trenazone, dienazone) is a synthetic anabolic-androgenic steroid of the 19-nortestosterone group. It was developed under the code RU-3118 and never marketed.
Based on rat and rabbit tissue bioassays, it has slightly lower affinity than nandrolone for androgen and progesterone receptors; trenbolone has similar androgen receptor affinity but several-fold higher progesterone receptor affinity. Its main practical role in the literature is as a chemical intermediate, including in routes to trenbolone and other steroids.

name: Norclostebol

angle.text: Norclostebol is a chlorinated nandrolone derivative described in 1957 and mentioned by physique readers for its anabolic class. It has no listed medical use and no human studies of muscle or appearance.

summary: A 1950s chlorinated nandrolone derivative with no listed medical use and no human studies.
note: Potency claims rest on a single source; no human trials.
currentQuick:
Norclostebol is a chlorinated derivative of nandrolone, described in 1957 and sold under brand names such as Lentabol.
Wikipedia lists no medical uses; the main published work concerns detecting its illegal use in cattle.
How it works: It is an anabolic-androgenic steroid reported as strongly anabolic and weakly androgenic.
Risks and caveats: No human safety studies were found.
deepLead:
Norclostebol (4-chloro-19-nortestosterone) is a synthetic anabolic-androgenic steroid derived from nandrolone, sold under names such as Lentabol; its acetate ester has been sold as Anabol 4-19. It was described in the literature in 1957.
Wikipedia lists no medical indications. Its norclostebol acetate form was reported on the European black market in the late 1990s for possible use in livestock, and a 2006 study identified its urinary metabolites in cattle.
